stem: Which description best matches the core pattern associated with histrionic personality disorder?

options.A: Pervasive excessive emotionality and attention-seeking behavior
options.B: Pervasive social detachment with restricted emotional expression
options.C: Preoccupation with orderliness, perfectionism, and control at the expense of flexibility
options.D: Persistent distrust and suspiciousness in which others' motives are interpreted as malevolent

rationale: Current NCBI/StatPearls material describes histrionic personality disorder as a pervasive pattern of excessive emotionality and attention-seeking behavior. Associated features can include inappropriate seductive or provocative behavior and rapidly shifting, shallow emotion. Therefore A is the best answer; B, C, and D describe other personality-disorder patterns.
educational_objective: Recognize the defining clinical pattern of histrionic personality disorder and distinguish it from other personality-disorder presentations.
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; article last updated 2024-06-20; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Introduction and DSM-5-TR diagnostic criteria: pervasive excessive emotionality and attention seeking; criteria include inappropriate sexually seductive/provocative behavior and rapidly shifting/shallow emotion
source_claim_supported: Histrionic personality disorder is characterized by pervasive excessive emotionality and attention seeking; rapidly shifting/shallow emotion and inappropriate seductive/provocative behavior are among recognized features.

correction_summary: Removed the family-member narrative and avoided diagnosing a client from a short behavioral vignette. Reframed the question around the disorder's defining pattern and replaced obvious distractors with plausible competing personality-disorder constructs.
audit_findings: A directly matches the authoritative description. B, C, and D correspond to schizoid, obsessive-compulsive, and paranoid personality patterns. No second-answer ambiguity, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved source conflict remains.
